questions.question_text: Explain how overgrazing may cause desertification. [4]

keywords_required: Overgrazing occurs when too many livestock eat/trample the vegetation.
This removes the protective plant cover and roots that bind the soil together.
The bare, exposed soil is then easily eroded by wind or rain.
Without vegetation, transpiration drops, leading to less rainfall, turning the semi-arid area into a desert.

questions.question_text: Describe three different characteristics of a coral reef. [3]

keywords_required: They are made of calcium carbonate secreted by tiny living coral polyps.
They are very colourful due to the presence of symbiotic algae called zooxanthellae.
They have immense biodiversity, acting as a habitat for thousands of marine species.

questions.question_text: Discuss how rivers can be managed to reduce flood risk. [7]

marking_scheme.rubric: AO2 and AO3: Discuss hard and soft engineering.
keywords_required: Hard engineering involves building physical structures (e.g. dams/reservoirs hold back water, floodwalls increase channel capacity).
Channelisation straightens the river to move water away quickly, though it may increase flooding downstream.
Soft engineering works with nature (e.g. afforestation increases interception and reduces surface runoff).
Floodplain zoning restricts building in high-risk areas, minimizing economic damage.
A good discussion must evaluate the pros/cons (e.g. hard is expensive and harms environment, soft is cheaper but may not prevent extreme floods).

questions.question_text: Suggest reasons why earthquakes in a Low-Income Country (LIC) often have a greater impact than earthquakes in a High-Income Country (HIC). [4]

marking_scheme.rubric: AO2: Suggest reasons for differing impacts.
keywords_required: Buildings in LICs are often poorly constructed and not earthquake-proof, leading to more collapses.
LICs have fewer emergency services and rescue teams, delaying life-saving treatment.
Poor infrastructure (roads/bridges) in LICs hinders the delivery of aid and medical supplies.
LICs may have a lack of public education/drills on what to do during an earthquake, leading to panic.

questions.question_text: Predict how climate change may impact global food production. [4]

marking_scheme.rubric: AO2 and AO3: Predict impacts on agriculture.
keywords_required: Increased frequency of droughts will reduce water availability for crops, lowering yields.
Rising temperatures may make some equatorial/tropical regions too hot for traditional farming.
Conversely, some colder/northern regions (e.g. Canada/Russia) may experience longer growing seasons, boosting production.
More extreme weather events (floods, hurricanes) will physically destroy crops and disrupt supply chains.
